subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be implemented as a scheduler-owned bounded verifier contract, a plugin-owned fail-capable hook, or deferred until a broader agent-verification API exists?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the proposed shell-based verifier changes command execution, retry, plugin API, persisted state, protocol, and security boundaries that automation should not choose by itself.

options.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
options.body: Define a first-class cron post-run verifier with typed config/state, command/plugin adapters, timeouts, output caps, redaction, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

options.title: Add plugin seam first
options.body: Expose a fail-capable cron post-run hook that can return pass/fail/retry/escalate decisions while keeping verifier implementation outside core.

options.title: Defer broader verification API
options.body: Keep this issue as a design tracker until maintainers settle a cross-surface agent outcome-verification architecture for cron and outbound delivery.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Define a first-class cron post-run verifier with typed config/state, command/plugin adapters, timeouts, output caps, redaction, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and is the strongest product/security routing candidate from the current issue discussion and cron history.
